root_cause.text: In the xfs attribute leaf block freemap update code during `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work`, expanding the entries array can leave zero-length freemap entries with non‑zero base, and the `_leaf_add` logic fails to update a freemap entry that begins midway into the newly appended entry; together these flaws create overlapping freemap entries that allow allocation of xattr name/value data on top of the entry array, causing data loss.
root_cause.evidence: The patch introduces an explicit check that zeros the base of any freemap entry with zero size and non‑zero base (`if (ichdr->freemap[i].size == 0 && ichdr->freemap[i].base > 0) { ichdr->freemap[i].base = 0; ... }`), which directly addresses the “zero-length freemap entry with nonzero base” problem. The CVE description further details that such entries, combined with the failure to update the overlapping freemap entry in `_leaf_add`, result in two entries with the same base but different sizes, leading to subsequent allocation over the entries array.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a potential bug by zeroing base of zero-length freemap entries to prevent overlapping freemaps in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block inside the loop over freemap entries that sets ichdr->freemap[i].base = 0 and ichdr->holes = 1 when ichdr->freemap[i].size == 0 and ichdr->freemap[i].base > 0.
intent_record.how: Prevents zero-length freemap entries with nonzero base from persisting, which avoids confusion in the _remove function that matches on base address and could create overlapping freemaps; also sets holes flag to trigger future compaction.

candidates.rationale: This line uses ichdr->freemap[i].size without ensuring that zero-length entries have their base zeroed, allowing non-zero base values to persist and potentially cause overlapping freemap entries when the entry array is expanded.

This update to usedbytes occurs after the loop that manipulates freemap entries; if the freemap has an overlapping entry due to a non-zero base on a zero-length entry, the accounting here will incorrectly reflect the available free space, contributing to potential allocation conflicts.
